entities.summary:
Psusennes I was the third pharaoh of the 21st Dynasty who ruled from Tanis in the Iron Age IB, between c. 1047 and 998 BC.

As a member of the royal family of Egypt, Psusennes I played a crucial role in maintaining the kingdom's power and influence during a time of significant upheaval in the ancient Near East.

Psusennes I's reign is notable for its military campaigns against neighboring regions, including the Sea Peoples and the Libyans, which expanded Egypt's borders and secured its position as a major world power.

His legacy can be seen in the numerous architectural and artistic achievements he commissioned during his rule, including the construction of several temples and monuments at Tanis, which showcased the wealth and grandeur of the Egyptian kingdom.

Despite his significant contributions to Egyptian history, Psusennes I's life remains somewhat shrouded in mystery due to the limited records available from ancient times. Nevertheless, his impact on the development of ancient Egypt and its place within the broader context of world history cannot be overstated.
